_transit_doc: Public transport (sim/transit, sim/commands/transit_commands.cpp). The 4.0's numbers, no source behind them yet: how near a click picks a stop, how far from a street a stop can stand, tracks joined, the most a track runs on a road, a metro entrance's reach, vehicles per line; a bus's dwell, at a terminal, the spacing, how far back it starts, at the stop, the street detour and pace away from the view; a train's dwell, speeds, acceleration and braking, the gap, cars and their length; level crossings: where a vehicle waits, when one closes, the room to the stop line.
_lanes_doc: What a lane's use asks of a driver (sim/traffic/lane_change.cpp, lane_graph.cpp). A bus lane takes buses alone, a line's bus and the city's own alike, and a bus off it takes it (the same code, art. 184, III, as law 13.154/2015 wrote it, in translation: 'on the lane or way of exclusive traffic, regulated with circulation meant for the vehicles of public collective passenger transport': the lane is that kind of vehicle's); a vehicle that is no bus enters it only to turn at the next junction or to reach a lot beside it, and leaves it otherwise: the Brazilian traffic code (CTB, law 9.503/1997), art. 184, in translation: 'To drive the vehicle: I - on the lane or carriageway on the right, regulated as of exclusive circulation for a given kind of vehicle, except to reach properties beside it or to turn right'. A continuous line between two lanes is not changed across, but where the road marks the entry: CONTRAN, the Brazilian manual of traffic signs, vol. IV, horizontal marking (Res. 236/2007), 5.5.1, in translation: the exclusive lane's line 'must be continuous all along, except on the stretches where entering or leaving the exclusive lane is allowed, or where there is an intersection or a turning movement, where the continuity line must be used'. params.lane_entry_m: the length of that stretch before a junction, the stretch the lane arrows stand on: the same manual, 9.1.1 (PEM), urban roads under 60 km/h: the first row of arrows d = 10 m before the end of lane changing, the second d1 = 30 m before it and the third, optional, d2 = 45 m before that (10 + 30 + 45 = 85 m); the road's paint breaks the bus lane's line over the same length (render/roads). params.approach_line_m: before a signal's stop line the lines between the lanes of one direction are continuous, and a driver changes lane across them only after waiting at the line: the same manual, the single continuous line dividing flows of one direction (LMS-1), principles of use, in translation: 'The LMS-1 must be used in the following cases: the approach of signalled intersections, with a length (L) of at least 15.00 m and at most 30.00 m, counted from the stop line, except where engineering studies point to a greater or a lesser one' (15 m here: a town's blocks are short); the rows of arrows stand before its start (9.1.1: d is counted from 'the start of the single continuous approach line').
_edge_doc: Traffic from the map's edge (sim/traffic/flow_rates.cpp, demand.cpp). A road that ends at the map's edge goes on past it: the street leaving that end starts the flow a street of its lanes carries at the demand's density, and the one arriving there ends every trip. params.edge_reach_m: a dead end this near the map's side is the map's edge (the game's own: about the widest road's width). params.edge_through_share: of the vehicles that come in at an edge, the share bound for another edge: Minnesota DOT, TH 14 New Ulm to Mankato corridor study, appendix B (a licence plate survey of 24,735 plates): 'About 20 percent of the passenger vehicle trips entering New Ulm pass directly through the town and about 80 percent of entering passenger vehicle trips stop in town for one or more purposes.'
_doc: Traffic and pedestrians (spec sim.md §5-§6). people_share: of the people the land use puts on the street; at this share the walking window holds at 16:00 about the 1000 walkers it always had, what the simulation step was measured with (61 of them within 150 m of the map's middle; the Roadcraft 4.0 counted 86 in a smaller city). Who walks: ped_child_share (of those out on foot; below the 19.8% under 15 of IBGE Censo 2022, the youngest do not walk the street, 9% measured in the Roadcraft 4.0), ped_elder_share (IBGE Censo 2022: 15.8% aged 60 or more), ped_elder_pace (Bohannon and Andrews 2011: women of 70-79 1.13 m/s, men of 20-29 1.36 m/s), ped_child_pace (1.23 m/s at 7-12 years, 10 m walk test, SPMRJ); ped_rest_fade_s: a quarter of the walk clip, the time to settle into standing. Anti-gridlock (CTB, Lei 9.503/97, art. 45: not even on green does a driver enter a junction where it may have to stop in the way of the cross traffic; a vehicle commits at its line only with room past the junction and the box clear): jam_seconds/release_every_s jammed-junction release, starve_seconds exit claim, detour_after_s detour at a full exit, reconsider_* route reconsideration in a full queue, bpr_gain congestion cost (the Bureau of Public Roads' travel time, Traffic Assignment Manual, 1964, with the load squared), tail_credit_* room a moving tail frees, gov_* fleet governor. Signals (CONTRAN MBST vol. V, 2022): opposite approaches share a stage, and each stage's green is actuated by the vehicles (cap. 7, green extension, optimum cut): a detection section signal_extension_s[lanes - 1] seconds of travel before the stop line (table 8.1: 4,1 / 1,8 / 1,0 / 0,6 / 0,4 s for 1 to 5 lanes, saturation flow 0,5 ucp/s per lane), each vehicle over it asking for that much more green; the minimum green is the largest of the vehicles' safety green signal_safety_green_s (5.14: never under 10 s), the queue between the section and the line signal_lost_start_s + (distance / signal_queue_spacing_m) x 3600 / signal_sat_flow_lane_h (7.3.1, Eq. 8.2: 3 s, 6 m, 1800 ucp/h per lane) and what the walkers it lets cross need: their safety green ped_safety_green_s (4 s), flashing red ped_reaction_s + crossing length / ped_clear_speed (5.7.2: 1,0 s and 1,2 m/s) and all-red ped_all_red_s (at least 1 s); the maximum green shares out the longest cycle signal_cycle_max_s (5.9: 120 s) left after the intergreens (7.3.3: the flows of a fixed plan are not known beforehand, so the stages get equal shares). The far (meso) traffic asks for green as it leaves a signalled lane, a saturation headway at a time. The intergreen after each green (5.7.1, Eq. 6.4-6.5): amber signal_reaction_s + v / (2 signal_decel) at the regulated speed (t_pr 1,0 s, a_ad 3,0 m/s²), at least amber_min_s up to amber_low_kmh, amber_min_mid_s up to amber_mid_kmh and amber_min_high_s above (3, 4 and 5 s), at most amber_max_s (5 s, the rest goes to the all-red); all-red (d2 + signal_vehicle_m) / v, d2 from the stop line past the junction and the far crosswalk, c 5 m, plus signal_ped_red_s (1 s) when walkers cross in the next stage. At the amber the driver stops unless the vehicle cannot be brought to rest safely (table 3.1): it stops when it can as that timing supposes (reaction, then signal_decel); of the others the amber only covers one that reaches the line before it ends, at its speed and braking at its class's b down to what its turn allows, so any other stops too while its class's b_emergency can do it. Pedestrians: trips of ped_trip_min_m..max_m between nodes; they cross arms along the middle of the painted zebra and vehicles stop behind the stop line (both from data/catalog/street_furniture.json crossing), walkers step off only with ped_critical_gap_s to spare and give a vehicle standing ped_courtesy_s its turn; ped_span_reach_m = heavy half width + 0.9 m either side of a lane. Walking speeds (Weidmann, Transporttechnik der Fussgaenger, IVT ETH Zuerich 1993: free speed 1,34 m/s, standard deviation 0,26 m/s): uniform between walk_speed_min and walk_speed_max, the same mean and deviation (1,34 -+ 0,26 x sqrt 3). Crowd (SUMO MSPModel_Striping, sumo.dlr.de/docs/sumo.html pedestrian.striping.*): the footway in ped_stripe_m stripes (stripe-width 0,64 m), a walker's centre at least half a stripe ped_margin_m off its edges (SUMO walks on the middle of its stripe); a body of radius ped_body_m (Fruin, Pedestrian Planning and Design, 1971: body ellipse 18 x 24 in, taken as the circle on its short axis, 0,46 m); a walker looks ped_look_m ahead, takes the stripe with the most room (ped_lateral_cost per metre aside, ped_keep_right_cost per metre off its own track, a better one only ped_stripe_gain_m better and after ped_stripe_hold_s), steps aside at ped_lateral_share of its pace and keeps ped_gap_m plus ped_headway_s behind a body (ped_accel to speed up again). The same stripes everywhere they walk: each walker sees every body near it (walkers in any mode, the street furniture's footprints) remapped into its own way's frame (SUMO's walking areas), on a sidewalk, round a corner (as wide either side of its line as the sidewalk it heads for, closing toward a place it must reach as fast as it steps aside, the leftmost ped_reserve_share up to ped_reserve_max_m left to those coming the other way: SUMO's reserve-oncoming on walking areas) and over a zebra (its right half only); a body moving slower than ped_moving_ms (under a body's width in 4 s) stands, one heading against its own way comes the other way; held up ped_jam_s on a sidewalk or round a corner, ped_jam_crossing_s on a zebra and ped_jam_narrow_s where its way itself holds one stripe only (the reference game's 20 s, 10 s and 1 s; SUMO's jamtime, jamtime.crossing and jamtime.narrow are 300, 10 and 1 s) it squeezes past walkers (never furniture) at ped_jam_share of its pace (SUMO and the reference: a quarter). At a crosswalk nobody is given a place (ped_kerb.cpp, the reference game's waiting): those about to cross wait on their own right of the zebra's middle line, out to kerb_wait_half_m from it or the zebra's edge (the left is where those from the other kerb arrive, so the two ways never meet in a crowd); a walker comes to an approach point back from the kerb, then walks a queue along the way across, where it stands at the kerb or behind those who wait, beside them where there is room, however long; with the leave it crosses from where it stands on a line parallel to the zebra's. Walkers appear on the sidewalks whose middle lies within ped_window_m of the camera and are taken away past ped_despawn_window_share of it, save whoever lies down or bleeds, who stays until they rise or die (pedestrians.cpp casualty): the 120 m beyond a 600 m window are half the longest segment (tuning road.max_seg_m, 112 m: 56 m) plus the 64 m the camera moves before the window is looked at again (traffic/window.cpp), so no walker is taken away at the edge it was just put on. Who walks with somebody (ped_party.cpp) is a walker of its own with the same trip, its side of the way beside its partner's, kept level by its pace alone, as the reference game walks its couples and families: near the one it came out with it walks at ped_company_catch of its pace when that one is more than ped_company_level_m ahead of it along its way and at ped_company_slow when as far behind. This game's own rule, which the reference has not (there a pair a crossing parts stays parted): farther apart than ped_company_wait_m (a few steps) the one ahead on their route stands and waits, off the crosswalks, while the other catches up; within ped_company_reach_m (the reference's 6 m) one goes over a crosswalk with the other, goes in at a door after it from where it stands, and leaves the street with it. A drawn vehicle stands on its path as on its wheels (sim/traffic/vehicle_pose.cpp): its middle half its length behind its front along the way it drove, its heading the path's chord heading_chord_m either side of that middle (the reference game's 1.5 m), and a lane change slides it to its new lane in lc_duration_s exactly. Junctions keep bodies apart by the bodies they sweep (sim/traffic/junction_sweeps.cpp, the reference game's rule and envelopes): three body classes body_small, body_car and body_heavy (length x width, a vehicle in the smallest that holds it), each swept along every connector's way (the end of the lane it leaves, its curve, the start of the lane it enters), its middle every sweep_step_m from a heavy body sweep_queue_back_m behind its line to its rear past the curve, a rectangle sweep_margin_m larger; two connectors conflict where any rectangles of theirs overlap, a body waiting until the other has cleared it, and a turn whose sweep reaches over a corner's footway is not driven by that class. A car going into or out of a lot closes every stretch of lane its body sweeps on its way (lane_closures.cpp sweep_body, the lorries' rule), parker_closure_margin_m beyond its body either way, once all those stretches are clear (lane_clear: nobody on them but whoever is behind its own body, nobody too near to stop short of them): going in, from where it stops until it stands on no lane, waiting at its gate's mark meanwhile; coming out, from where it still stands on none until it is on its lane's list (lot_traffic.cpp). A junction on automatic, before its flows have been measured, runs on signals when it has signal_arms arms or more, or three where one road carries signal_lanes lanes or more both ways (two each way, an avenue's: road_profiles.json lanes); a T of narrower streets goes by rank (junction_control.cpp decide; the reference game's rule). Two arms whose outward directions meet under through_pair_dot (at least 120 degrees apart: the reference game's main road legs) are one road going through; the road a junction is on is the pair of them whose lesser priority is the highest (junction_control.cpp main_arms): without a signal it has the way and every arm joining it gives way (with every arm on it, or none in line, nobody has it: by movement and from the right, CTB art. 29 III c); the player's signs and the flows take its straightest pair, and the green wave runs along it. Read by native/src/api/traffic_loader.cpp into TrafficParams. Distances in metres, times in seconds, speeds in m/s unless the key says km/h.

styles._doc: What changes with a city's regional style (session-rules.md, section 10). traffic_hand: the hand of the road traffic keeps to (sim/traffic/parking_lanes.cpp, parking_sources.cpp read it as a side number); right only for now, the lanes are laid out for it, and a style that says left is refused at boot.

brazil._doc: CTB art. 29, I: circulation on the right.

europe._doc: To fill from the Vienna Convention on Road Traffic (1968), art. 10, and the Convention on Road Signs and Signals; each state chooses its side: the United Kingdom, Ireland, Malta and Cyprus drive on the left and would be styles of their own.

_kerb_doc: Errands at the kerb (kerb_stops.cpp), the 4.0's numbers, no source behind them, but kerb_end_clear_m: CTB art. 182 I forbids stopping within 5 m of the cross street's kerb line, to which a car's length and the crosswalk (the 4.0 kept 30, and on map 0, its lanes 50 m long on average, nobody ever stopped): share of cars setting somebody down (18 % of the 45 % with a passenger), picking somebody up, trucks on a delivery and how long the mate is away; clear of the street's ends, the planning margin, the stretch it needs, where along it, the room ahead; where the door is along the body and out from it, the clear round its swing and on the footway, its seconds to open and shut, to leave or take a seat, the pace to the door, the give-up time, the pause before opening, how far a walker is looked for and called from.
_lorry_doc: Lorries to the docks (sim/traffic/lorry_traffic.cpp, yard.cpp). lorry_radius_m: the rear axle's path at full lock of AASHTO's SU-30 design vehicle (Green Book: centreline radius 38 ft, wheelbase 20 ft: sqrt(38^2 - 20^2) ft). lorry_rear_m: the body's middle ahead of the rear axle of the Volkswagen Delivery 11.180 the truck is drawn after (agents.json truck: 8.485 long, front overhang 1.26, wheelbase 4.6). lorry_plan_work: the units of work (sim/traffic/way_search.h) a tick spends planning a yard, 1 ms of it at the unit's 0.048 µs measured on 2026-11-05 on a bench of the planner since removed (git keeps it before commit 18782f55): the 4.0's planning under a millisecond a tick (lorryDocks.ts PLAN_BUDGET). The rest are the 4.0's and have no outside source: how far the search reaches, the stop before a gate, the unloading time.
_junction_doc: Who goes first at a junction and how a signal runs (sim/traffic/junction_gate.cpp, junction_admission.cpp, junction_control.cpp, signal_plan.cpp, signal_demand.cpp, signal_timing.cpp, turn_classes.cpp). gap_right_s, gap_straight_s, gap_left_s, gap_main_left_s: the gap a driver who gives way asks before a movement that goes first, by its own turn: the Highway Capacity Manual's base critical headways at a two-way stop, as the PTOE study guide's table gives them (open-exam-prep.com/study-guides/ptoe/managed-lanes-tsmo-its/unsignalized-intersections-roundabouts): minor-street right turn '6.2 s (2-lane major)', minor-street through '6.5 s (2-lane major)', minor-street left turn '7.1 s (2-lane major)', major-street left turn '4.1 s (2-lane major)'; a turn back takes the left's (the manual has no row for it: a choice). The headway holds the manoeuvre itself, so the gate asks the greater of it and the vehicle's own clearing time (the sweeps' clear arc at gap_clear_share of its pace through, at least gap_clear_least_ms) plus gap_clear_margin_s (choices), counting a head that stands as moving at gap_slow_ms. gap_temper: how far a driver's temper moves its gap (a choice). gap_impatience, gap_impatience_most_s, gap_floor_s: the gap falls with the wait (Polus, Shmueli Lazar and Livneh, 'Critical Gap as a Function of Waiting Time in Determining Roundabout Capacity', Journal of Transportation Engineering 129(5), 2003, its abstract: 'an increase in drivers' average waiting times reduces the average accepted gap and, consequently, the critical gap'; the paper's model is a logistic curve between a most and a least gap, and gives no rate a second: the rate, its cap and the floor are choices). Past claim_after_s a driver claims the turn. Who goes first with no sign: the Brazilian traffic code (CTB, law 9.503/1997) art. 29, III, in translation (its own words: doc/work/junctions.md, Sources): a) where only one flow comes off a highway, whoever travels on it (the player's control 'none': a highway's flow first); b) at a roundabout, whoever circulates on it (a mini-roundabout: who comes from the left); c) elsewhere, whoever comes by the driver's right. zip_ready_m, zip_patience_s: where two lanes run into one their heads take turns: the lane that went last leaves the next place to the other's head while that head is within zip_ready_m of its line or standing, and for no longer than zip_patience_s (choices). ring_meter_share: nobody comes onto a ring from outside while its vehicles, each in its standing room slot_m, with one more would pass this share of its lanes' length, so those on it can leave (a choice). straight_dot, turn_back_dot: a movement within 30 degrees of straight on is straight, one past 150 degrees a turn back (cosines; choices; the road a junction is on goes straight through it however it bends). The signal: its stages pair opposite approaches (CONTRAN MBST vol. V), an approach alone joins a stage it meets nobody in, a turn that gives way all through its stage gets a stage of its own on demand: turn_stage_green_s its least green, turn_stage_most_s its most (choices). signal_starve_cycles: a stage asked for and unserved for this many cycles runs next; signal_queue_weight: the queued vehicles that double a stage's claim (choices). ped_wait_limit_s: a walker who waited this long at a kerb has its stage next (a choice under the ceiling two Brazilian capitals hold a walker's wait at a signal to, one and a half minutes, as their press gives it; the reports' own words: doc/work/junctions.md, Sources). ped_hold_limit_s: a green is not ended over people still on its crossings for this long from when it would have ended (CTB art. 70: the walker who began to cross has the way to the end; the limit is a choice). ped_flash_s: the walkers' stop lens flashes once in this time while who is on the crossing finishes (a choice: the source of the flashing's rate was not found). ped_yield_temper: a driver whose temper is over this gives no way to who waits at a kerb (a choice). bus_extension_s: where the player puts buses first, a bus near its line holds its green this long past its most (RTIG, 'How does traffic signal bus priority work', RTIG-T065, as a search gives it: 'Stage Extensions are where the current green stage is extended, usually to a preset maximum (typically 3-5 secs)').
_flow_doc: The far traffic as flows (sim/traffic/street_flows.cpp) and the window that follows the view (window.cpp). The link model is the Link Transmission Model as tabenchmark's design note ADR-016 writes it (tabenchmark.readthedocs.io, 'ltm: Yperman (2007) link transmission model'): 'sending(k) = min(N_up(t_{k+1} - L/vf) - N_dn(t_k), q_max·dt)', 'receiving(k) = min(N_dn(t_{k+1} - L/w) + kappa·L - N_up(t_k), q_max·dt)', with 'dt <= min(L/vf, L/w)' (a street shorter than that takes one step). At a node each approach is served in proportion to its capacity (Tampere, Corthout, Cattrysse, Immers 2011, Transportation Research Part B 45(1) 289-309, its abstract: 'an oriented capacity proportional distribution of the available supply over the incoming links of a node'). flow_wave_kmh: how fast a queue's tail moves back, from the triangular diagram of TU Delft's Traffic Flow Theory, chapter 5 ('a free speed of 80 km/h, a capacity of 2000 veh/h/lane and a jam density of 150 veh/km/lane': 2000 / (150 - 25) = 16 km/h). The room a standing car takes is slot_m, a lane's capacity follows from the two: v w / ((v + w) slot_m). Choices, no source: flow_dt_s (the model's step, s), flow_green_share (the share of the hour an approach into a signal or a stop has), flow_links_per_tick (the streets and nodes of flow work a tick: a step is spread over the ticks of its second, so a tick's cost does not grow with the map), flow_origin_queue (cars a lane waiting to start on a street before more are not made), flow_admit_per_tick (cars made in the window a tick), flow_speed_step (a street's speed is told to the render again when it moved by this share). The window: its radius is the view's reach (how far the view sees on the ground from the point it looks at: the farthest corner of the frame cast on the ground, a corner over the horizon counting as beyond every window) x window_view_share, never under window_min_m nor over meso_window_m; it moves when the camera is past window_recentre_share of it and is resized when the view outgrows it or shrinks under window_shrink_share of it (choices). window_min_m is the few blocks a close view keeps as detailed traffic (the reference game's least is 300 m): the detailed traffic is stepped for what the picture shows, not for a fixed 1100 m; the bays are still read and drawn within park_window_m, but a lot sends and takes cars, and a dock takes a lorry, only while its street is inside this window (lot_demand.cpp bay_served, lorry_traffic.cpp call), and the walkers' window is ped_window_m, never past this one (window.cpp walk_window_m); beyond it the streets carry the flows' far cars; with no camera (a test with no view) the window stands at meso_window_m. A trip's mean length is trip_decay_m (the exponential's mean): the share of a street's traffic that ends its trip on it and how often its sides send one out follow from it.
_drive_doc: How each driver drives (sim/traffic/driver.h, vehicle_speed.cpp, lane_change.cpp). temper_*: how far a driver's temper (-1 timid .. +1 pushy, two uniform draws) moves its class's acceleration, comfortable brake, headway, standing gap, patience, politeness and lane change threshold: a design choice: the spread between drivers was searched and no table of it was found (Kurtc and Treiber, arXiv 1610.03124, calibrate the model driver by driver on NGSIM's trajectories, 'different parameter values can be attributed to each individual driver-vehicle unit', and show the spreads only as figures). follow_coolness: the share of the constant-acceleration heuristic in the following law (Kesting, Treiber, Helbing 2010, arXiv 0912.3613: realistic values 0.95 to 1.00, the paper uses 0.99). jerk_up, jerk_brake: how fast the pedal moves easing on and in ordinary braking, m/s3 (ISO 15622's limit as Hadjigeorgiou and Timotheou give it, arXiv 2506.04685: 'The ISO 15622:2018 standard for adaptive cruise control specifies that the average acceleration over one second should be limited to 2 m/s2, while deceleration should not exceed -3.5 m/s2. Additionally, it mentions a limit on negative jerk of -2.5 m/s3.'; the same rate easing on is a choice); follow_crawl_ms: under it a driver lifts off at once. bend_lat_max, bend_lat_fall, bend_lat_min: the lateral acceleration a driver accepts in a bend, max - fall x speed, never under min, m/s2: a line through AASHTO's maximum side friction factors of low-speed urban streets as Iowa DOT's Design Manual, 2B Superelevation, lists them from the Green Book's Table 3-7 (as a search of the manual gives the table; the page itself refused a fetch): 0.32 at 15 mph, 0.27 at 20, 0.23 at 25, 0.20 at 30, 0.18 at 35, 0.16 at 40, 0.15 at 45, which times g are 3.14 m/s2 at 6.7 m/s down to 1.47 at 20.1 m/s; 4.0 - 0.125 v with the floor 1.4 is within 0.2 m/s2 of each row; bend_heavy_share: the share of it a heavy body uses (a choice: a heavy vehicle rolls over far sooner than a car, UMTRI, 'Rollover of Heavy Commercial Vehicles', 1999, as a search gives it: 'The rollover thresholds of passenger cars are virtually always greater than 1 g', a loaded heavy truck's often well below 0.5 g; no source gives the share drivers use); bend_temper: how far temper moves it; bend_least: the curvature (1/m) under which nobody slows (a 500 m radius); bend_keep_share: the share of a street's sharpest curvature its bend's stretch is kept to. lc_politeness: MOBIL's politeness of an ordinary driver (Treiber's page of the model, traffic-simulation.de/info/info_MOBIL.html: realistic in ]0, 0.5], with a threshold of 0.2 m/s2 and a safe braking of 4 m/s2 as typical); lc_signal_s: the indicator runs this long before a lane change (CTB art. 35 asks the signal ahead of the move and gives no figure: a choice); lc_crawl_ms: the slowest a driver goes to fit the changes its turn needs; lc_slope: the most a body moves sideways per metre it drives in a lane change (about 19 degrees of heading: a choice; at speed the change takes lc_duration_s of travel, a shallower path); signal_ahead_s, signal_ahead_m: a turn is signalled this long, and at least this far, before its line (Texas Transportation Code 545.104: not less than the last 100 feet). classes: a bus pulls away at 1.2 and brakes at 1.5 m/s2, what standing passengers bear (Karekla and Fang 2021, as cited in Frontiers in Future Transportation 2023, doi 10.3389/ffutr.2023.931780: 1.0 to 1.5 m/s2 for a comfortable balance standing); a loaded truck 0.9 and 1.8: under the most it can do (S. Washburn's freight curriculum, 4.1.3, swash17.github.io/FreightCurriculum/acceleration.html: 'For heavily loaded trucks, in the range of 60-80,000 lbs, maximum acceleration rates from rest (i.e., a stopped condition) and on level terrain are on the order of 3.5 ft/s/s', 1.07 m/s2) and, as every class's comfortable brake, well under the 11.2 ft/s2 (3.4 m/s2) AASHTO designs stopping distances with, a rate some 90% of drivers brake at or above (as FHWA's and the states' manuals give it).
_classes_doc: [a, b, b_emergency, headway T, min gap s0, share of the speed limit, length, half width] per type: sedan, hatch, suv, van, pickup, moto, bus, truck (drivers.ts ARCH, traffic/state.ts), bicycle (SUMO vehicle type defaults, vClass bicycle: accel 1.2, decel 3, emergencyDecel 7, tau 1, minGap 0.5, length 1.6, width 0.65; bike_speed_kmh its desiredMaxSpeed 20 km/h). Where a street has no cycle lane a bicycle rides on the edge of the carriageway (CTB art. 58), its middle bike_edge_m from the lane's edge: half the 1,2 m minimum operating width of AASHTO's Guide for the Development of Bicycle Facilities, 2012.
_zones_doc: Weights by base zone [none, residential, commercial, industrial, mixed] (traffic.ts:938-947; peds ZONE_PULL).
_people_doc: People on foot by kind of place [home, shop, work, civic]. people_kind_m: per 100 m of street at full bustle; people_busy: how busy each kind is at each hour from midnight, a row a kind (the Roadcraft 4.0's day as drawn by hand, with no survey behind it); people_working, people_purchasing: percent of those aged 15 and over at each hour (BLS American Time Use Survey, table A-3; United States data, the default style's), with work_stay_h and errand_stay_h the stays that turn them over; zone_kinds: what each base zone's land is, a row a zone.
